source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 7 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 7 Find the interior angles of the kite whose vertices are \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(2, 3)\), \(C(4, 0)\) and \(D(2, -3)\).
blocks.explanation:
Phir chaar sides wali shakal ke interior angles, sirf coordinates se.
Pehle direction: \(B\) upar aur \(D\) neeche hai, is liye \(A \to B \to C \to D\) clockwise chalta hai. Hum ulti tarteeb \(A \to D \to C \to B\) lenge jo anticlockwise hai.
Slopes nikal kar har vertex par Theorem 7, agle vertex wali side se pichhle vertex wali side tak.
Aakhir mein jama \(360^\circ\) check.
Kite woh shakal hai jis mein do do sath wali sides barabar hon; yahan to chaaron sides barabar nikalengi, is liye hamare jawab mein aamne saamne ke angles barabar aane chahiye.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(2, 3)\), \(C(4, 0)\), \(D(2, -3)\).
Maloom karna: interior angles \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\).
Tareeqa: anticlockwise tarteeb \(A \to D \to C \to B\). \(A\): \(AD\) se \(AB\) tak; \(D\): \(DC\) se \(DA\) tak; \(C\): \(CB\) se \(CD\) tak; \(B\): \(BA\) se \(BC\) tak.

Sides ke slopes
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 0}{2 - 0} = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{0 - 3}{4 - 2} = -\dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[m_{CD} = \dfrac{-3 - 0}{2 - 4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[m_{DA} = \dfrac{0 - (-3)}{0 - 2} = -\dfrac{3}{2}\]
Kyun: do points se slope. Aamne saamne ki sides ke slopes barabar hain, yani woh parallel hain.
Ek aur faida: kyunke sirf do hi slopes hain (\(\frac{3}{2}\) aur \(-\frac{3}{2}\)), har angle mein wahi numbers aayenge, sirf order badlega.

Angle \(A\) (\(AD\) se \(AB\) tak)
\[\tan A = \dfrac{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{1 + \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{-5/4} = -\dfrac{12}{5}\]
\[A = 180^\circ - 67.38^\circ = 112.62^\circ\]
Kyun: neeche \(1 - \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{5}{4}\); \(3 \div \left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) = -\frac{12}{5}\). Tan negative, angle obtuse; \(\tan^{-1}\frac{12}{5} = 67.38^\circ\).

Angle \(D\) (\(DC\) se \(DA\) tak)
\[\tan D = \dfrac{-\frac{3}{2} - \frac{3}{2}}{1 + \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}\]
\[= \dfrac{-3}{-5/4} = \dfrac{12}{5}\]
\[D = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{12}{5} = 67.38^\circ\]
Kyun: \(m_1 = m_{DC} = \frac{3}{2}\), \(m_2 = m_{DA} = -\frac{3}{2}\); minus over minus plus, angle acute.

Angle \(C\) (\(CB\) se \(CD\) tak)
\[\tan C = \dfrac{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{1 + \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}\]
\[= -\dfrac{12}{5}\]
\[C = 112.62^\circ\]
Kyun: \(m_1 = m_{CB} = -\frac{3}{2}\), \(m_2 = m_{CD} = \frac{3}{2}\); bilkul wahi numbers jo \(A\) par the.

Angle \(B\) (\(BA\) se \(BC\) tak)
\[\tan B = \dfrac{-\frac{3}{2} - \frac{3}{2}}{1 + \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}\]
\[= \dfrac{12}{5}\]
\[B = 67.38^\circ\]
Kyun: \(m_1 = m_{BA} = \frac{3}{2}\), \(m_2 = m_{BC} = -\frac{3}{2}\); wahi numbers jo \(D\) par the.

Tasdeeq:
\[112.62^\circ + 67.38^\circ + 112.62^\circ + 67.38^\circ = 360^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Chaaron sides ki lambai \(\sqrt{13}\) hai, is liye yeh kite asal mein rhombus hai, aur rhombus ke aamne saamne ke angles barabar hote hain, jaisa aaya.
Khulasa: do angles obtuse (\(A\), \(C\)) jo \(x\)-axis par pare vertices hain, aur do acute (\(B\), \(D\)) jo upar neeche ke nukeele kone hain; figure bana kar dekhein to bilkul aisa hi lagta hai.
